note: Wave 13 — clearing the source defects. Nine rows that had been left unknown because their cited document could no longer establish anything are now resolved against a current source, and seven of them have had source_url repointed. The MRI row carries the most consequential finding in the whole backfill: NSF skipped the entire FY2026 competition. UG3 is a correction to this session's own earlier reading.

updates.status_evidence: NSF announced on 1 July 2025 that it would not accept new MRI proposals in the scheduled FY2026 window (15 October – 14 November 2025), returning any without review, and “anticipates accepting new proposals again during the next submission window, scheduled for October 15 – November 16, 2026”. A skipped cycle with an announced next window, not a wind-down.
updates.notes_append: IMPORTANT CONTEXT 2026-09-18: NSF skipped the entire FY2026 MRI competition to fund more of the FY2025 cohort. Anyone planning around MRI should know the next window opens 15 October 2026. Note also that NSF's own pages are inconsistent here — solicitation NSF 23-519 is labelled both “Active funding opportunity” and “Status: Archived” depending on the view, which is why this row needed the announcement rather than a page label to settle it.

updates.program_name: NSF GOALI - Grant Opportunities for Academic Liaison with Industry
updates.status_evidence: NSF's Engineering directorate maintains a live GOALI page; GOALI funding “can be requested in conjunction with a regular proposal submitted to a standing program of NSF, or as a supplemental funding request to an existing NSF-funded award”, with instructions in the PAPPG.
updates.notes_append: SOURCE REPOINTED 2026-09-18: was NSF 10-580, which NSF marks archived. GOALI is a proposal type rather than a standing solicitation, which is why it has no current solicitation number of its own.

updates.status_evidence: The Department of Education's International Resource Information System presents DDRA as a current programme (CFDA 84.022) that “provides grants to colleges and universities to fund individual doctoral students to conduct research in other countries”, with programme brochure and performance-report templates posted.
updates.notes_append: SOURCE REPOINTED 2026-09-18: the ed.gov programme page now 404s. CAVEAT: the newest competition that could be confirmed is FY2025 (Federal Register, 30 October 2024, applications due 15 January 2025, ~$3,000,000 subject to congressional action). IRIS presents the programme as current and posts no termination notice, which is what `active` records — but no FY2026 or FY2027 competition was found, so this row deserves an early re-check.

updates.program_name: Sea Grant John A. Knauss Marine Policy Fellowship
updates.status_evidence: “MEET THE 2026 FELLOWS” and “Interested in hosting a Knauss executive or legislative fellow in 2027?” — a current class and a forward-looking 2027 call.
updates.notes_append: SOURCE REPOINTED 2026-09-18: the previous deeper URL returned an empty body to both a text fetch and a rendering browser. Resolved with a rendering browser.

updates.program_name: William G. "Bill" Bankhead Jr. & David Coley Cancer Research Program
updates.status_evidence: The programme is established in section 381.922, Florida Statutes, and Florida reports that “In fiscal year 2026-27, a total of $70 million is available for Florida cancer innovation research” across the King and Bankhead-Coley programmes.
updates.notes_append: SOURCE REPOINTED 2026-09-18: the previous URL returned HTTP 404.

updates.program_name: Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers (PECASE)
updates.status_evidence: PECASE continues across 14 participating agencies; the most recent cohort was announced in January 2025, when nearly 400 scientists and engineers received the award. NSF and DOE both maintain current PECASE pages.
updates.notes_append: SOURCE DEFECT STANDS 2026-09-18: the row's source_url is still a January 2012 ONR news release about 2011 awardees. It was left in place because PECASE is conferred across many agencies and this row is filed under the DoD stream — choosing a replacement is an editorial call, not a mechanical one. Candidates: nsf.gov/honorary-awards/pecase or science.osti.gov/About/Honors-and-Awards/PECASE.

updates.program_name: Research Supplements to Promote Re-entry, Re-integration into, and Re-training in Health-Related (Biomedical and Behavioral) Research Careers - Re-entry component
updates.status_evidence: NIH lists re-entry supplements among its current administrative supplement programmes: “Full or part-time mentored research training experiences for individuals with high potential to reenter, reintegrate into, or retrain in an active research career”. Page last updated 9 April 2026.
updates.notes_append: SOURCE REPOINTED 2026-09-18: the row cited NOT-OD-23-170, which has expired. The programme runs through the Administrative Supplement parent announcement and individual institutes (NHLBI, NINDS, NIGMS, NCI all post their own pages).

updates.program_name: NIH Phased Milestone-Driven Awards (UG3/UH3 and UH2/UH3)
updates.status_evidence: “As part of a bi-phasic approach to funding exploratory and/or developmental research, the UG3 provides support for the first phase of the award”. The activity-code page exists and carries no retirement notice.
updates.notes_append: CORRECTION 2026-09-18: two earlier reads of NIH's activity-code index reported UG3/UH2/UH3 as absent. The direct activity-code page exists and describes UG3 as current, so the index summary was incomplete rather than the codes retired. Lesson recorded in FINDINGS: absence from a summarised index is weaker evidence than a direct page check, and should never by itself move a row toward terminated.

updates.program_name: FINESST — Future Investigators in NASA Earth and Space Science and Technology
updates.status_evidence: ROSES-25 programme element F.5 FINESST “solicits proposals from accredited U.S. universities and other eligible organizations for graduate student-designed and performed research projects”, with proposals due 14 July 2026.
updates.notes_append: SOURCE REPOINTED 2026-09-18: the row cited ROSES-2022 Amendment 70, whose proposals were due in February 2023.
